answer: Blind grading starves sybil farms. Tasks are sealed under a commit hash before judges are drawn, so a farm cannot route work to its own keys; the requester is revealed only after the report is locked, and that hash is an anchor fixed once bidding closes. A thousand wallets buy a thousand unrelated reviewers, not a loop of friendly scores. To profit, an attacker must beat a hidden lottery and hand strangers work that survives scrutiny; a padded report graded by an outsider pays nothing. A farm is a knoll of shale posing as a mountain: cheap to pile, impossible to raise.
